newsitem.title: GERMANY: WORLD COFFEE STOCKS SEEN FALLING IN 1997/98 SEASON.
newsitem.headline: WORLD COFFEE STOCKS SEEN FALLING IN 1997/98 SEASON.

text.p: Global coffee stocks in the 1997/98 (Oct/Sept) season are forecast to fall to over 31 million bags from opening stocks of 32.36 million on Oct 1, 1997, figures from German trader Bernhard Rothfos GmbH showed.
The ratio of world stocks to global consumption at the end of the new season would be 31 percent, down from 32.5 percent a year earlier, it said in its quarterly digest.
The ratio had been falling since October 1995, Rothfos noted.
Producing countries in 1997/98 were seen reducing their coffee stocks to 17.48 million bags from 20.44 million on Oct 1, 1997 and compared with 24.38 million on Oct 1, 1996.
Consuming countries were expected to build up theirs to 13.95 million from 11.92 million at the start of the 1997/98 season and compared with 8.27 million on Oct 1, 1996.
Importing countries' stocks at the end of 1996/97 would represent 8.2 weeks of coverage, Rothfos said.
The forecast for consumer country stocks of 13.95 million at end-1997/98 was assuming coffee was exported without restrictions arising from international agreements in the 1997/98 crop year.
